points.description: Says empirical equations are derived from experiments, observations or measured data (rather than theory).
points.partial_credit: 1 mark if vaguely stated, e.g. 'based on practice/experience' or 'formulas used in practice' without mention of data/experiments

points.description: Mentions they have no rigorous mathematical/theoretical proof or derivation behind them.
points.partial_credit: Award if they are described as not derived theoretically; otherwise all or nothing

rubric.notes: Full marks (2) for the core idea that the equations come from experiments or observed data; a missing mention of no mathematical proof costs at most 0.5. Give part marks for vague answers such as 'based on experience' or 'approximate formulas used in practice'. Give 0 for wrong or unrelated answers, e.g. defining them as exact theoretical equations.
